what: SHA-256 of the PCM samples of Minesweeper's recorded sounds (the WAV's data chunk, i.e. the file from byte 44 on; the 44-byte header is not hashed because it carries no sound).
why: The recording itself is not committed: media files (.wav) are refused by the repository's pre-push guard, and a fixture a person can open is not needed, only a strict proof that the sounds are unchanged. Re-recorded for the proportional 1x font: the title now draws one frame later, so the tones start 0-6 samples (<=0.14 ms) later in the recording window. Every burst keeps its pitch (within 0.1%) and length (+-1 sample), and the final mine starts at the same sample with the same length, so no sound changed; only its phase within a frame moved. Re-recorded again after the table shrink: every cue keeps its pitch (within one zero crossing) and length (within one sample) and moves by at most 1 sample; the mine is a NOISE burst seeded from the key-wait counter, so its samples differ when instruction timing changes even though its length, swing and pulse count are the same. The recording is deterministic run to run.
command: node cli/cloadm.js -m dragon64 --program minesweeper --frames 30 --poke $3003=$5E,$ED --type ' ' --frames 20 --wav OUT.wav --type ' ' --frames 20 --type '{RIGHT}{DOWN}F' --frames 20 --type '{UP}{RIGHT}{RIGHT}' --frames 5 --type F --frames 10 --type F --frames 10 --type ' ' --frames 60 --wav-stop
listen: To hear it, run that command with OUT.wav set to a path outside this repository (the same sequence tests/games.test.js runs). Nothing is written into the repo.
note: Phase shift is expected and documented; the sound itself is unchanged.
